prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production animation extension of an ADOPTED pixel game character, not a redesign. The attached sheet is the approved design and poses at nearest 4x; use its first standing pose as exact identity, palette, scale and proportions. Same adopted middle-aged Japanese martial artist uncle: swept white crest over dark hair, white eyebrows, gray stubble, charcoal/ivory sleeveless gi, ochre belt, dark sandals. Body ~42 native pixels tall. Exact approved face, no redesign.
Create only these NEW motion poses: 4 columns x 2 rows. Top row four distinct alternating walking phases near leg forward, far passing, far leg forward, near passing, calm upright posture. Bottom row (4) blocked-hit recoil alive, (5) composed recover, (6) quick backward withdrawing step facing RIGHT with guard relaxed, (7) opposite-leg withdrawing step. No weapons, no glowing effects. Bow/punch/kick already exist; do not regenerate them.
Transparent RGBA background, equal grid cells, generous transparent gutters, consistent full-body scale and ground baseline, complete feet and limbs. Clean chunky square pixel clusters for a small game sprite enlarged into the output, same muted palette, 1-pixel native dark brown contour, upper-left illumination. No smooth airbrushed illustration, no labels/grid/text/background/ground shadows/additional people. Same head and face in every cell. Meaningful limb changes, never just translated duplicates. Output only the motion sheet.
